units.title: Evaluation Protocol I: Platelet vs Coagulation Bleed Table, Lineage Chart, Count-Based Bleeding Risk & Drug-Induced Thrombocytopenia
units.sec: Evaluation Protocol I: Platelet vs Coagulation Bleed Table, Lineage Chart, Count-Based Bleeding Risk & Drug-Induced Thrombocytopenia
units.guide:
Protocol step 1 (p173): platelet bleed starts immediately after trauma whereas coagulation bleed is late; platelet type is mucosal (gum, epistaxis, menorrhagia, intra-operative) with petechiae <3 mm and purpura 3–10 mm; coagulation type is joint (haemarthrosis), muscle (m/c ilio psoas), hematoma and large solitary ecchymotic patch >10 mm; sex male = female vs male > female.
Step 2 lineage: single lineage → 1° platelet bleeding; trilineage (leukemia, aplastic anemia, MDS) → platelet related bleeding. Platelet-count risk: >20,000/µL no bleeding, <20,000/µL bleeding +ve, <10,000/µL severe (GI, cerebral); red purpura in pharynx and retinal bleed indicate risk.
Step 3 drug-induced thrombocytopenia: chemotherapy/alkylating agents dose related; procainamide and gold produce autoantibody; heparin → immune complex with PF4.

units.title: Evaluation Protocol II: Anticonvulsant/Gp IIb-IIIa/NSAID/Quinine/Penicillin Table, Hypersplenism, Smear & ITP Summary Flowchart
units.sec: Evaluation Protocol II: Anticonvulsant/Gp IIb-IIIa/NSAID/Quinine/Penicillin Table, Hypersplenism, Smear & ITP Summary Flowchart
units.guide:
Step 3 table continues (p174): anticonvulsants (carbamazepine, phenytoin, valproate) and NSAIDs have no mechanism listed ('–'); Gp IIb/IIIa inhibitors act by drug-specific antibody (abciximab within 24 hours, plus eptifibatide and tirofiban); quinine induces antibody; penicillin acts as a hapten-dependent antibody.
Step 4 hypersplenism: sequestration of platelets, seen in liver disease; of the three arms of ↓ platelet count, destruction of platelet is m/c; the marrow arm produces no platelets, RBC or WBC.
Step 5 smear: schistocytes → rule out HUS/TTP; normal smear with a few giant platelets (rare) goes with ITP. The summary flowchart ends: platelet-type bleeding → single-lineage with normal RBC/WBC → not drug induced → no hypersplenism → normal smear → ITP.

units.title: Immune Thrombocytopenic Purpura I: Causes, Gp IIb/IIIa & Ib/IX Antibody Pathogenesis, Clinical Signs & Investigations
units.sec: Immune Thrombocytopenic Purpura I: Causes, Gp IIb/IIIa & Ib/IX Antibody Pathogenesis, Clinical Signs & Investigations
units.guide:
ITP basics (p175): AKA Werlhof's disease, not seen in elderly; primary or secondary (SLE, RA, H. pylori, HIV, HCV); IgG antibody-mediated destruction with antibodies against Gp IIb/IIIa and Ib/IX plus inhibition of platelet release from megakaryocytes.
Clinical: mucocutaneous bleeding when the count is <20,000/µL (example gum bleed); petechiae and purpura are non-palpable and non-blanching, unlike palpable branching vascular purpura; photographs show petechiae/purpura, oral petechiae and ecchymosis.
Investigations: normal smear with a few giant platelets; Coombs test only for Evans syndrome or CVID with AIHA plus thrombocytopenia; marrow shows increased megakaryocytes and precursors, done for atypical findings (splenomegaly), first episode >60 years, or failure to respond to steroids.

units.title: ITP II: Features Inconsistent with ITP, Duration-Based Classification & First-Line Treatment (Steroids, IVIg/Anti-D)
units.sec: ITP II: Features Inconsistent with ITP, Duration-Based Classification & First-Line Treatment (Steroids, IVIg/Anti-D)
units.guide:
Features inconsistent with ITP (p176): fever, pallor, jaundice, subconjunctival haemorrhage, bleeding into joints, splenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, predominant giant platelets, red-cell morphological abnormality, WBC abnormality. Duration: <3 months newly diagnosed, 3–12 months persistent, >1 year chronic.
Treatment aim: raise platelets to 30,000/µL; >30,000 wait and watch, <30,000 ± bleeding treat; children have a self-limiting course.
Adults first line: oral prednisolone full dose × 2 weeks then taper, ± IVIg/anti-D (indications: surgery, life-threatening bleeding, platelets <10,000/µL, relapse). Anti-D binds Rh antigen and is taken up preferentially by the spleen sparing platelets; prerequisites are a spleen and Hb >10 mg/dL.

units.title: ITP III: Second-Line Therapy, Follow-Up & Qualitative Platelet Disorders (Causes, Defect Types, PFA-100 & Aggregation Test)
units.sec: ITP III: Second-Line Therapy, Follow-Up & Qualitative Platelet Disorders (Causes, Defect Types, PFA-100 & Aggregation Test)
units.guide:
Second line in relapse (p177): rituximab + dexamethasone; thrombopoietin analogues eltrombopag (oral) and romiplostim (s/c); splenectomy; azathioprine. Follow-up: counts rise in 2–4 days.
Qualitative platelet disorder = bleeding with a normal platelet count; acquired causes are uremic bleeding (m/c) and drugs, besides inherited causes. Defect types: adhesion (Gp Ib-IX → Bernard-Soulier, and vWD), granulation (α granule → grey platelet, δ granule → Hermansky-Pudlak), activation/aggregation (Gp IIb-IIIa → Glanzmann, and afibrinogenemia).
Investigations: PFA-100 is a screening test with prolonged aperture closure time >80 sec; the aggregation test is the gold standard, weak agents (ADP, epinephrine) giving two waves and all other agents one wave; primary aggregation releases no granules, secondary aggregation releases thromboxane A2 or granular ADP.

units.title: Aggregation Curves (Biphasic vs Monophasic), Ristocetin Agglutination Test + aPTT Logic, Bleeding Time & vWF Functions
units.sec: Aggregation Curves (Biphasic vs Monophasic), Ristocetin Agglutination Test + aPTT Logic, Bleeding Time & vWF Functions
units.guide:
Normal aggregation curves (p178): biphasic with ADP and epinephrine (primary then secondary wave), monophasic with collagen, arachidonic acid and ristocetin.
RAT checks adhesion: negative in Bernard-Soulier syndrome and vWD, positive means normal adhesion. A negative RAT is followed by aPTT (common and intrinsic defect): prolonged aPTT → vWD with low factor VIII, normal aPTT → BSS. Bleeding time is elevated and obsolete.
vWF functions: platelet adhesion and transport of factor VIII. Aggregation interpretation strip: ADP primary wave, collagen deficient, ristocetin normal → granule defect (storage pool defect loses the second ADP/epinephrine wave).

units.title: Optical Density Traces: Aggregation Defect vs BSS/vWD vs Storage Pool (Granule) Defect Interpretation
units.sec: Optical Density Traces: Aggregation Defect vs BSS/vWD vs Storage Pool (Granule) Defect Interpretation
units.guide:
Glanzmann curves on p179 show absent aggregation with all agonists except ristocetin and are labelled 'Aggregation defect'; 'Aggregation defect : No waves seen' while 'granule defect : Primary wave seen in ADP & epinephrine'.
Optical density test: normal agglutination/adhesion lowers optical density (↓ optical density).
Three interpretation panels: aggregation defect (A: RAT +ve, B: aggregation –ve), BSS or vWD (A: RAT –ve, B: agglutination wave +ve), and storage pool/granule defect (A: agglutination wave +ve in ADP).

units.title: Glanzmann Thrombasthenia, Afibrinogenemia, Bernard-Soulier Syndrome, Megathrombocytosis & Drug-Induced Qualitative Bleeding
units.sec: Glanzmann Thrombasthenia, Afibrinogenemia, Bernard-Soulier Syndrome, Megathrombocytosis & Drug-Induced Qualitative Bleeding
units.guide:
Platelet disorders (p180), set against 'Fibrinogen —thrombin time→ Fibrin': Glanzmann thrombasthenia is autosomal recessive with normal thrombin time, GpIIb-IIIa defect (fibrinogen receptor lost), RAT +ve, normal platelet count, prolonged BT and recurrent bleeding or heavy menstrual bleeding.
Afibrinogenemia has a prolonged thrombin time. Bernard-Soulier syndrome is autosomal recessive with Gp Ib-IX deficiency, RAT negative (adhesion defect) and a smear showing megathrombocytosis with mild thrombocytopenia.
Drug-induced qualitative bleeding: aspirin, beta lactams, dipyridamole/theophylline, ticlopidine/clopidogrel and dextran.

units.title: Von Willebrand Disease I: vWF Gene/Structure Domains, ADAMTS13 Processing, Functions & Types
units.sec: Von Willebrand Disease I: vWF Gene/Structure Domains, ADAMTS13 Processing, Functions & Types
units.guide:
vWD is the m/c congenital bleeding disorder, gene on chromosome 12p (p181). Structure domains: A → adhesion (binds GpIb-IX), D3 → carries factor VIII, C → aggregation.
Physiology: megakaryocyte-derived vWF monomers → dimers → HMW multimers which circulate and are degraded by ADAMTS 13; endothelial vWF is stored coiled in Weibel-Palade bodies and released uncoiled after endothelial injury. Functions: platelet adhesion and carriage of factor VIII (T½ 2 → 12 hours).
Types: Type 1 (m/c), Type 2 (2A, 2B, 2M, 2N) and Type 3 (rare).

units.title: Von Willebrand Disease II: Type 1 vs Type 3 Table, Type 2 Subtypes (2A/2B/2M/2N), Acquired vWF & Management
units.sec: Von Willebrand Disease II: Type 1 vs Type 3 Table, Type 2 Subtypes (2A/2B/2M/2N), Acquired vWF & Management
units.guide:
Type 1 vs Type 3 (p182): Type 1 = 85% incidence, autosomal dominant, partial semiquantitative defect, platelet bleed without coagulation bleed (factor VIII unaffected) and ↑aPTT, 2nd decade; Type 3 incidence is not printed ('–'), autosomal recessive, complete quantitative, severe platelet and coagulation bleed, <5 years.
Type 2: 2A AD with absent HMW multimers (platelet bleed); 2B AD gain of function at the A-site with platelet trapping (thrombocytopenia); 2M AD loss of function at the A-site (adhesion, platelet bleed); 2N AR loss of function at the D3 site (factor VIII carriage, pseudohemophilia, presentation in females). Pseudo-vWD = loss of function of GpIb-IX.
Acquired vWF: aortic stenosis (shear stress, ↑ cleavage), myeloproliferative/PCRV (adherence, ↑ cleavage), IgG/IgM paraprotein (immune mediated), hypothyroidism (↓ synthesis). Management: vWF concentrate or desmopressin (best, v2 stimulation, contraindicated in 2B, IV or intranasal, tachyphylaxis and SIADH), used only on bleeding, with anti-fibrinolytic add-on.

units.title: DIC I: Clinical Approach by aPTT/PT/Platelet Combinations (Factor XII/XI/Hemophilia A & B/vWD/LAC/Liver/Warfarin) & Etiology
units.sec: DIC I: Clinical Approach by aPTT/PT/Platelet Combinations (Factor XII/XI/Hemophilia A & B/vWD/LAC/Liver/Warfarin) & Etiology
units.guide:
Clinical approach table (p183): prolonged aPTT with normal PT and platelets — no bleeding implies factor XII, HMW kininogen or prekallikrein deficiency, mild bleeding implies factor XI (hemophilia C), severe bleeding implies hemophilia A/B (clotting factor bleed, chronic proliferative synovitis, muscle symptoms) or vWD (platelet-type bleed, RAT negative); prolonged aPTT with reduced platelets implies antiphospholipid syndrome from lupus anticoagulant.
Prolonged aPTT and PT with reduced platelets implies liver disease (all clotting factors except VIII, dysfibrinogenemia) or DIC; normal aPTT with prolonged INR implies warfarin (vitamin K epoxide reductase inhibition, gamma carboxylation of glutamic acid residues of II, VII with shortest t½ 6 hr, IX, X), factor III or factor VII deficiency.
Etiology: sepsis (m/c), APML, placenta and amniotic fluid, adenocarcinoma (lung, colon, prostate), trauma, pancreatitis, burns, massive transfusion, Kasabach-Merritt syndrome.

units.title: DIC II: Pathogenesis Chain, ICU Monitoring, Purpura Fulminans, Investigations (FDP vs D-Dimer) & Management
units.sec: DIC II: Pathogenesis Chain, ICU Monitoring, Purpura Fulminans, Investigations (FDP vs D-Dimer) & Management
units.guide:
Pathogenesis (p184): stimulus → endothelial activation → tissue factor release → continuous and excessive thrombin formation → consumption of platelets and clotting factors → bleeding plus secondary hyperfibrinolysis with fibrinogen trapping.
ICU monitoring: ARDS (saturation, chest examination, X-ray), DIC with haemorrhagic spots, myocarditis (tachycardia, hypotension unresponsive to fluids, ↑ troponin I). Clinically bleeding exceeds thrombosis with reduced anticoagulant factors; oozing at venipuncture sites, petechiae, ecchymosis; fibrinolysis exceeds antifibrinolysis; purpura fulminans is severe DIC with microvascular thrombosis and skin necrosis.
Investigations: ↓ platelets, ↑ aPTT, ↑ PT, ↑ FDP (most sensitive), ↑ D-dimer (most specific), fragmented RBCs, ↑ TT, ↓ fibrinogen. Management: treat the cause, cryoprecipitate (VIII, vWF, fibrinogen, XIII)/FFP/platelets, EACA; drotrecogin alfa and heparin are obsolete; liver disease is the differential diagnosis.
